mentions.name: Repere
mentions.description: An in-browser data explorer for datasets too large for spreadsheets but too small to justify spinning up SQL. It runs entirely client-side on DuckDB-WASM with no server uploads or accounts, representing transformations (filter, join, aggregate, pivot) as a visual DAG of lazy view nodes so DuckDB executes the full pipeline on demand. It supports CSV/Parquet/Excel inputs, a SQL editor with schema-aware autocomplete, pivot tables with drill-down to underlying rows, and sessions exported as files or shareable URLs with the pipeline encoded in the hash, including granular control over whether data files are embedded (with upload-to-restore for large files). Pipelines can be replayed on new data with schema validation, and files never leave the browser since it is a static website. Work in progress, planned to be open sourced under MIT.
mentions.problem: Datasets too large for spreadsheets but too small to justify spinning up SQL, with privacy concerns since files should never leave the user's browser
mentions.audience: People analyzing datasets too large for spreadsheets but too small to justify setting up SQL, who share and replay pipelines with colleagues
